_comment: Figure manifest for the Axial SWS site. 'source' is repo-relative and is READ ONLY - build_figures.py never modifies, moves, or commits source files. 'page' is 1-indexed. 'width' overrides defaults.width for dense multi-panel figures. 'badge' marks a figure that predates the Grade-3/windowcheck pipeline so it is never silently shown as current.

pre_windowcheck.label: PRE-WINDOWCHECK
pre_windowcheck.tooltip: Generated before the 2026-07-24 undersized-window fix. Not from the current Grade-3 production chain.

partial_stations.label: 3 OF 6 STATIONS
partial_stations.tooltip: Pools AXCC1 + AXEC1 + AXEC2 only. A six-station regeneration is pending.

older_inversion.label: OLDER RUN
older_inversion.tooltip: From the July 2026 raw-quality inversion, not the Grade-3 windowcheck run. Shown because no Grade-3 checkerboard was produced.

stale_threshold.label: THRESHOLD OUT OF DATE
stale_threshold.tooltip: Diagram shows Q_w ≥ 0.5; production Grade 3 is Q_w ≥ 0.75. Needs redrawing.

degenerate_fit.label: FIT DEGENERATE
degenerate_fit.tooltip: The fitted inflation azimuth collapses onto the fixed background azimuth and A blows up, producing a discontinuity. Read the scatter, not the curve.

figures.title: Geological structure of Axial Seamount
figures.caption: Caldera setting over shaded bathymetry. White dotted line: outline of the main magma reservoir (MMR); orange and red contours: the MMR roof at 1.5 km and 1.25 km depth. Hatched grey polygons: the east and west ring faults. Black lines: rift zones and dikes, running north and south from the caldera. Green outlines: the 2015 lava flows. Stations are coloured by instrument — yellow for short-period (AS1, AS2, EC1, EC3), blue for broadband (CC1, EC2). The Pacific–Juan de Fuca plate boundary runs through the caldera.

figures.title: Caldera setting and relocated seismicity
figures.caption: Axial Seamount caldera. Native-colour bathymetry, every processed event in the MLdd catalog (deduplicated by origin time across the six stations), and the six OOI Regional Cabled Array OBS stations.

figures.title: Measurement distributions (1/5)
figures.caption: Distributions of every numeric output column: φ, δt, their errors, Q_w, SNR, rectilinearity, incidence, dominant period, and the per-event chosen filter band.

figures.title: Quality vs. source depth
figures.caption: Log-count 2-D histograms of Q_w against source depth, one panel per station. No Q_w cut applied — Q_w is the axis.

figures.title: Back-azimuth, depth & quality — AXAS1
figures.caption: Back-azimuth against source depth and against Q_w. Baseline cleanup only, so the full Q_w < 0 null population stays visible — this is the panel that tests the Wüstefeld (2010) prediction that true nulls cluster at discrete back-azimuths while false nulls scatter.

figures.title: Splitting measurement pipeline
figures.caption: End-to-end workflow: waveform retrieval and QC, dominant-period estimation, MFAST-style dynamic windowing, LQT rotation on the PyKonal-traced S incidence, Silver & Chan eigenvalue minimisation over the window/lag/angle grid, and DBSCAN clustering with Teanby (2004) representative-variance selection. Note: the "Final Filtering" box in this diagram gives Q_w ≥ 0.5 as its example threshold; the production Grade-3 cut is Q_w ≥ 0.75. The diagram's text is baked into vector glyph paths and it has no generating script, so correcting it means rebuilding the figure by hand.

figures.title: A well-constrained split
figures.caption: AXEC2, event 298_74456, 2015-04-21. Q_w = 1.000, SNR = 23.3, rectilinearity = 0.999, incidence = 14.6°, φ_err = 7°, δt = 0.03 ± 0.005 s. The highest-ranked measurement across all 497 pre-eruption batches.

figures.title: A well-constrained null
figures.caption: AXEC2, event 74_18279, 2015-03-02. Q_w = −0.984, at the discretised floor — the most confident 'no splitting' the metric can express. δt = 0.01 s with δt_err = 0.005 s, so the null is not confounded by a noisy measurement.

figures.title: Cycle skipping
figures.caption: AXEC2, event 238_59346, 2015-04-06. Q_w = 0.000 (indeterminate), δt = 0.16 s against T_dom/2 = 0.0345 s — 4.6× over threshold, with a broad non-unique error-surface minimum. This is the case that motivates the δt ≤ T_dom/2 cut in the Grade-3 filter.

figures.title: Fast direction by eruption-relative period
figures.caption: Six station rows × seven periods (before, during, and five equal-event-count post-eruption bins), grouped by western and eastern caldera. Each panel carries N, mean φ ± SE, and the axial cosine similarity to that station's pre-eruption panel.

figures.title: Fast direction by equal-inflation period
figures.caption: The same figure with the five post-eruption bins carrying equal amounts of Central Caldera inflation rather than equal event counts — the physically motivated companion, and the newest of the rose set.

figures.title: Fast direction by year
figures.caption: Fourteen annual columns: pre-2015, syn-2015, post-2015, then 2016 through 2026.

figures.title: Back-azimuth decomposition, by period
figures.caption: Each cell's central rose ringed by six 60° back-azimuth sub-roses, testing whether the fast direction is a back-azimuth sampling artefact rather than a property of the medium.

figures.title: AXAS1 — equal-inflation periods
figures.caption: Western caldera (ASHES). Post-eruption bins carry equal physical inflation. AXAS1 and AXAS2 reference the ASHES BOTPT, whose record begins 2017-08-15.

figures.title: AXCC1 — equal-inflation periods
figures.caption: Central caldera. No real data exists 2015-03-01 to 2015-04-28 — the sensor was unlevelled by pre-eruption inflation and reset after eruption onset.

figures.title: Uplift vs. fast direction — AXAS1
figures.caption: φ against Central Caldera uplift, matched 30-day rolling windows on both axes, fitted with the atan2 vector-sum model: a fixed regional tectonic stress vector plus a fixed-orientation inflation vector whose magnitude grows with uplift. Turnover u0 is auto-estimated per station by a free-location logistic pre-fit.

figures.title: Uplift vs. fast direction — AXCC1
figures.caption: AXCC1's fit returns A ≈ 42 against 0.4–20 at every other station, producing a near-discontinuous rather than smooth transition. Treat this fit, and the AXCC1 arrow on the inflation-vector map, with more caution than the other five.

figures.title: Regional mean φ vs. uplift — Western Caldera
figures.caption: AXAS1 + AXAS2 pooled into a single western-caldera mean fast direction, against the same Central Caldera BOTPT uplift. Measurements are collapsed to per-calendar-day circular means before the 30-day roll, so each day counts once for the region. Fitted inflation azimuth β = 125.2°, A = 1.02, r = 0.52 over N = 2209. Note the turnover is auto-estimated at u₀ = 0.05 m, i.e. pinned to the low edge of the uplift range, so the fitted curve is a decay across the observed span rather than a completed S-transition.

figures.title: Regional mean φ vs. uplift — Eastern Caldera
figures.caption: AXEC1 + AXEC2 + AXEC3 pooled into an eastern-caldera mean, against Central Caldera uplift. The cleanest of the three regional fits: a steady rotation from about 160° to 130° with β = 247.3°, A = 1.27, r = 0.69 over N = 3064. AXEC2's 2021-07 to 2022-09 unlevelled window (520 measurements) is dropped from the pool rather than flagged, since a known instrumental drift would otherwise pull the regional average. The turnover sits at u₀ = 2.63 m, the upper edge of the observed uplift, so this span samples the near-linear part of the curve.

figures.title: Regional mean φ vs. uplift — Central Caldera
figures.caption: AXCC1 alone, against the Central Caldera uplift it sits on. The scatter is real and shows a rotation with inflation, but THE FITTED CURVE SHOULD NOT BE READ AS A RESULT: the fit returns β = 170.0°, exactly the fixed background azimuth α = 170°, with A = 41.7 against 0.4–1.3 at every other station or region. With β collapsed onto α the two stress vectors are collinear, the vector sum degenerates, and the atan2 argument flips sign across the turnover — which is the vertical jump visible at u₀ = 1.03 m. This is the same failure mode noted for AXCC1 in inflation_vector_map_sixstations_ccal.py, and it needs resolving before AXCC1's inflation-vector azimuth is used for anything.

figures.title: Fitted inflation-vector azimuths
figures.caption: Grayscale bathymetry with each station's fitted inflation-vector azimuth β as a red arrow. Reuses compute_all_station_fits() from the fit above, so the map cannot drift from the fits. AXCC1's arrow inherits the caveat noted on its panel.

figures.title: Uplift vs. φ, unfitted — AXAS1
figures.caption: The deliberate no-fit view: pre-eruption deflation and post-eruption re-inflation as two panels pivoting at zero uplift, 90-day windows. Complementary to the fitted version, not superseded by it.

figures.title: Central Caldera BOTPT — de-tided depth and uplift
figures.caption: De-tided seafloor depth 2015-01-22 to 2026-05-15, and metres of uplift referenced to the post-eruption minimum, with the five equal-inflation period boundaries marked. Total re-inflation ≈ 2.6 m.

figures.title: ASHES BOTPT — de-tided depth and uplift
figures.caption: The western-caldera geodetic reference used by AXAS1 and AXAS2. Record begins 2017-08-15.

figures.title: Delay time through the eruption — AXEC2
figures.caption: δt as a moving-window density against time, with a ±48 h eruption zoom. Filtered Q_w > 0.5, φ_err < 20°, δt_err < 0.04 s. No Grade-3 equivalent of this figure exists yet — see the note below.

Fractional anisotropy across the caldera
figures.caption: All six stations pooled, each measurement assigned to its ray's arc-length lateral midpoint on a 0.25 × 0.25 km grid, minimum 10 measurements per cell, one row × seven periods. Fractional anisotropy solved from a² + 2xa − 4 = 0 with x = 2·T_travel/δt. Note that AXEC2's 2015–2021 half lacks event coordinates, so only its 2022–2026 data contributes.

figures.title: Fast direction across the caldera
figures.caption: The fast-direction quiver companion to the panel above, on the same grid and periods.

figures.title: Percent anisotropy through time — AXEC3
figures.caption: φ against time in 21-day windows with a ±24 h eruption zoom, and δt/T_travel × 100 against time.

figures.title: Inverted anisotropy strength
figures.caption: Joint six-station 2-D inversion, one row × seven equal-inflation periods. Quad-tree blocks to a 0.25 km minimum, d = Gm with δt_r = Σ s_b L_rb, Sherman–Morrison covariance whitening, bounded weighted least squares. Blocks failing checkerboard recovery are greyed and hatched.

figures.title: Inverted fast direction
figures.caption: Per-block fast polarisation from the same inversion, averaged in doubled-angle space.

figures.title: Checkerboard resolution test
figures.caption: Input against recovered checkerboard, λ = 1 km, joint six-station, Q_w ≥ 0.7. From the July 2026 run — the Grade-3 inversion produced strength and quiver output but no checkerboard, so this stands in until that is regenerated.
